EU duty: GSP+, and the condition the UK no longer applies

Pakistan holds EU GSP+ status, valid to 2027, under which the EU cuts duties to zero on more than two thirds of beneficiaries’ tariff lines. Apparel MFN duty runs roughly 8.4–12%, so on a covered garment GSP+ removes that line entirely.

The catch is origin, and we would rather say so up front. The EU applies rules of origin to clothing that are stricter than the UK’s. Britain dropped its two-stage requirement for apparel on 1 January 2026, so a garment cut and sewn here from imported fabric now enters the UK at 0%. The EU has made no equivalent change, and EU eligibility still turns on where the fabric itself was produced.

So we will not quote you a flat 0% into Germany the way we can into Britain. We check your garment’s commodity code and the origin of its fabric, then tell you the actual rate before you commit — because a supplier who promises duty-free and is wrong does not pay the correction, you do, at the border. German import VAT at 19% applies regardless and is normally reclaimable as input tax if you are VAT-registered.

EU imports carry 19% German VAT, plus apparel duty of 8.4 to 12% unless a trade preference removes it - and Pakistan holds EU GSP+, which zero-rates most covered lines. Both are bundled into DDP quotes with compliant paperwork. What German buyers ask us about first is compliance and sustainability, and it is where we put the work: a documented 4-stage QC process, organic cotton and recycled polyester programmes through our sustainable collection - documentation included, ready for the EU's textile regulations tightening through 2027.

FAQ: Manufacturing for German Brands

Do you handle EU customs, duty and VAT?

Yes, we ship DDP and handle the paperwork. On duty: Pakistan holds EU GSP+ status, which removes the tariff on most covered lines rather than the 8.4 to 12% an origin with no preference pays. The EU conditions that on rules of origin for clothing, and those are stricter than the UK equivalent, so whether a given order qualifies depends on where its fabric was produced. We confirm that per order before quoting instead of assuming it. German import VAT at 19% applies either way and is normally reclaimable if you are VAT-registered.

Are your fabrics tested for EU compliance?

We source export-grade tested fabrics and supply the test documentation for retailer and marketplace onboarding; fabric test reports available on request.

Can you produce sustainable garments?

Yes - organic cotton, recycled polyester, hemp, Tencel and bamboo garments through our dedicated sustainable line, relevant to the EU textile rules arriving from 2027.

How long is delivery to Germany?

Express courier 3-5 business days; sample-to-delivery is typically 3.5-5 weeks, or 26-34 days by sea to Hamburg for large orders.

What is the minimum order for EU brands?

50 pieces per style per colorway - full size run included. Most EU startups begin with 100-150 total pieces across 2-3 styles.
